content.comment_body: Thank you for your communications library, it's been very helpful. Using it, I can monitor a networked [article_no], start and stop processes, read inputs and outputs, and check device status. I have a question: is it possible to compile a program for [article_no], save it to a file, and then load it into the device memory remotely via Ethernet? For my affordable home automation project, being able to update customer devices over the internet would be a big advantage, eliminating the need to visit each site in person. I'm experimenting with this feature using your library and would like to connect with you about it.

Hello, if your [product_name] with [article_no] has a static IP address, you can try connecting to it in [product_name] V7 using that IP address. Make sure to forward port 10001 for the device. Although I'm not certain it will definitely work, there is a reasonable chance. Hope this helps.
Hi, I've shared a short guide on a site that shows how to accomplish what you're asking for: [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Community members are exploring how to update [product_name] program files remotely over Ethernet to simplify maintenance and support for home automation projects. While monitoring and control tasks are functioning effectively using the communication library, users remain uncertain if program compilation and file transfer for remote memory loading can be achieved reliably. Posts suggest possible methods but do not provide an agreed-upon or officially supported solution, highlighting unclear documentation and partial understanding of remote update capabilities.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want the ability to compile and transfer program files to [product_name] devices using Ethernet, making it possible to update customer installations remotely without needing onsite visits.
